title: Lior and the Will
premise: True-crime podcaster Lena Thackeray has spent a decade documenting the unsolved disappearance of Marisol Vega, the coldest case in Harrow's Bend — until a confession letter arrives postmarked the day after the town patriarch's funeral, naming three accomplices still living there. As Lena investigates, they discover the letter was written by someone inside their own found family of case archivists, and that the killer has been feeding them curated evidence for years. In the end, Lena stages a fake statute-expiry deadline to force a confession on record, exposing the killer but choosing to hand the evidence to Marisol's estranged daughter rather than the compromised local police.
about_author: C. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. They live in a converted records office and claim to alphabetize their regrets.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Opening the confession letter at the archive desk, Lena finds it postmarked the day after Edmund Hale's funeral — yet describes details never made public. The emotional beat is vertigo: ten years of careful distance collapsing in one envelope.

chapters.title: The Alphabetized Dead
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A tour of the podcast archive reveals how meticulously Lena has filed Marisol Vega's case — and how someone else has been quietly correcting their files for years. Beat: unease dressed as gratitude.

chapters.title: Harrow's Bend Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: Dual POV with deputy Ray Okafor. Lena returns to town and interviews witnesses whose memories have been gently reshaped over a decade. Beat: the horror of discovering memory itself can be edited.

chapters.title: Three Names
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The letter names three accomplices; two are dead, one is beloved diner owner Ruth Calloway. Lena sits across from her, saying nothing. Beat: the weight of an unasked question.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Circle
chapters.summary: POV of Priya Nair, Lena's closest collaborator. We meet the found family of volunteers who built the case database — including quiet, brilliant Theo Marsh, who knows every file by heart. Beat: warmth with hairline cracks.

chapters.title: What the Funeral Buried
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At Hale's grave, Lena learns the patriarch ran the search party that 'failed' to find Marisol. His will contains a sealed envelope addressed to the sheriff. Beat: dread compounding.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Ray Okafor's POV. The legal clock: charges must be filed within weeks. Ray wants to help but the department buried the original file. Beat: justice versus institution.

chapters.title: The Corrected File
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Comparing digital timestamps, Lena proves someone edited the archive remotely — from inside the Circle. Beat: betrayal as a slow dawning.

chapters.title: Ruth's Silence
chapters.summary: Ruth Calloway's POV. Ruth remembers the night Marisol died and why she stayed silent: Hale owned her debts, her house, her daughter's future. Beat: complicity born of desperation.

chapters.title: Theo Explains Everything
chapters.summary: Theo Marsh's POV. Charming, meticulous, Theo walks Lena through the case flawlessly — too flawlessly, answering questions Lena hasn't asked aloud. Beat: admiration curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Left
chapters.summary: Marisol's daughter Camila Vega's POV. Camila arrives in town furious that strangers profit from her mother's ghost. She and Lena clash, then recognize each other as fellow keepers of grief. Beat: friction becoming alliance.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Records Room
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Someone breaks into the archive and burns the physical originals — but the digital backups survive because Priya moved them off-site weeks ago, on anonymous advice. Beat: the trap tightening around its maker.

chapters.title: A Letter Too Many
chapters.summary: Priya Nair's POV. Priya admits receiving 'research help' emails for years from an account traced to the funeral home. Beat: the found family realizing they were instruments.

chapters.title: The Sheriff's Sealed Envelope
chapters.summary: Ray Okafor's POV. Hale's will envelope is opened: his own confession as accessory, naming the fourth participant only as 'T.M.' Beat: the past refusing to stay filed.

chapters.title: What Theo Kept
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Searching Theo's cottage, Lena finds Marisol's missing locket and a decade of drafts — confessions written and rewritten, never sent. Beat: pity warring with revulsion.

chapters.title: Camila's Choice
chapters.summary: Camila Vega's POV. Camila learns the truth and must decide whether her mother's story belongs to the law, the podcast, or herself. Beat: reclaiming narrative ownership.

chapters.title: The Deadline Gambit
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. With two days before the statute expires, Lena leaks a false story that the case is being dismissed, baiting Theo into one final act of control. Beat: cold clarity after years of feeling.

chapters.title: Confession, On Record
chapters.summary: Theo Marsh's POV. Lured to the archive by the fake dismissal, Theo delivers a full confession to what he believes is a dead microphone — while Ray records from the next room. Beat: the killer undone by his need to be the best-informed person in any room.

chapters.title: Why He Stayed
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Interrogation aftermath: Theo killed Marisol accidentally at seventeen, then spent ten years curating the case to keep it beautiful, unsolved, his. Beat: grief for the boy he was, justice for the girl he erased.

chapters.title: Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Ray Okafor's POV. The department moves to bury the recording; Ray resigns and hands copies to Camila instead. Beat: choosing people over institutions.

chapters.title: The Last Episode
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena airs the finale — not as spectacle, but as testimony, giving Marisol her name back and crediting Camila as co-author. Beat: release, and the end of keeping secrets alphabetized.

chapters.title: Unfiled
chapters.summary: Camila and Lena's alternating POV, brief. Months later, the archive becomes a community memory project run by Camila; Lena keeps one box unalphabetized — letters from listeners still searching for their own missing. Beat: hope as an open file.
